data.description:
## Description
**What**: Add a synthetic end-to-end test exercising three scenarios across the emit/read/validate/verifier path: (a) HAPPY PATH — brainstorm 3-SC epic, preplanning extends and reassigns (deferred=false), impl-plan extends, read.sh returns zero _conflicts, validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent and zero lightweight_pending; (b) PARALLEL-SPRINT DUPLICATE-DETECTION — two dispatches register a test_artifact against the same intent_id, validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity AND a dedup warning fires (d566 integration or a synthetic stand-in); (c) ORPHAN-DETECTION — 1-SC epic with --lightweight preplanning and no impl-plan stage yields lightweight=true/deferred=true, validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending, and completion-verifier produces a non-empty Intent Allocation Findings section naming the SC.
**Why**: Proves the stages compose end to end and protects the loop against regression.
**Scope**:
- IN: the three-scenario synthetic e2e test and its fixtures.
- OUT: changes to the stage emitters, read, validate, hook, or assistant (consumed, not modified).

## Done Definitions

- The happy-path scenario drives brainstorm, preplanning, and implementation-plan emitters and asserts read.sh returns zero _conflicts and validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent and zero lightweight_pending ← Satisfies: sc-10
- The parallel-sprint scenario registers two test_artifact entries against the same intent_id and asserts both validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity and a dedup warning fires ← Satisfies: sc-10
- The orphan-detection scenario runs --lightweight preplanning on a 1-SC epic with no implementation-plan stage and asserts lightweight=true with deferred=true, validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending, and the completion-verifier output names the unresolved SC in a non-empty Intent Allocation Findings section ← Satisfies: sc-10
- The synthetic end-to-end test runs in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the test passes ← Satisfies: sc-10

## Considerations

- [Live-verified] SC10 asserts runtime end-to-end behavior across multiple stages, so it runs in a configuration-isolated environment rather than inheriting the developer's runtime.
- [Dedup stand-in] The d566 test-quality reviewer may not be shipped; scenario (b) uses a synthetic stand-in invocation for the dedup warning while still requiring both signals to fire.
- [Shell hygiene] Any new .sh fixture/test file sets the executable bit on creation.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, I want a synthetic end-to-end test covering happy-path, parallel-sprint duplicate detection, and orphan detection, so that the full allocation loop is regression-protected.
